input.label: Selected complete form migration edition

definitions.reference: Exact selected scope and supported route

settings.reference: Exact selected scope and supported route

responses.reference: Exact selected scope and supported route

uploads.reference: Exact selected scope and supported route

workflow.reference: Exact selected scope and supported route

downstream.reference: Exact selected scope and supported route

assets.provenance: Exact original export/source/version locator; no tokens
assets.content_state: COMPLETE|PARTIAL|REDACTED|UNASSESSED (separate from file presence; default UNASSESSED)

input.discovery_manifest: Complete original commons.discovery.cohort-manifest.v1 object. Each selected table must map to a PRESENT CSV asset; only paths are rewritten to retained originals.

file_comparisons.reference: Exact byte-equivalence interpretation; differing IDs remain byte differences

parent.reference: Required explicit parent interpretation when asset_class differs from responses

attachments.reference: Explicit owner-selected canonical link; never inferred from filename

attachment_comparison.reference: Approved equivalence; parent keys, ordinal, byte count and full digest always compared

notes: Each original CSV table is bound to an exact present asset; full original engine manifest and migration selection retained.
CSV repeated sections and historical field revisions require explicit source modeling. Every selected row participates.
Body presence is separate from content coverage; unknown coverage remains UNASSESSED.
Parent record is the one-based data record after header; parent raw key values are matched before attachment equivalence.
All original and received intake fields are preserved, including extra supported-route/reviewer/decision metadata. A saved revised intake creates a new native project.
Every selected upload original requires an explicit parent link; no filename or ZIP-path inference.
Source and target comparison table assets must match pair_classes and their respective source/target side.
Attachment parent table original must have the attachment's side and explicitly selected parent class.
Coverage tracks every selected original asset independently; each uncovered asset receives an asset_coverage finding.
